subject: [EXTERNAL] Production latency + errors impacting BluePeak (possible network path)
messages:
From: Carla Reed <carla.reed@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: BluePeak NOC <noc@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: production latency spikes + 500s from Redwood Inference

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing severe performance regressions on our production integration with Redwood around 03:00 UTC this morning. Symptoms: p95 latency jumped from ~250ms to 2.5–4.8s, error rate on API responses is ~6.9% (mostly 502/504s), and overall throughput dropped by ~35%. This is affecting our user-facing inference calls (large language chat flows).

For context: we are on Redwood Dedicated running in us-west-2, peered with our VPC (vpce-0a1b2c) via a transit gateway. We didn't intentionally change anything on our side, but our NOC is seeing increased packet loss and intermittent DNS failures resolving model-host.redwood.net.

This is a P1 for us — we have a board-level update in ~2 hours and need immediate investigation. Can you confirm whether there were any infra changes, region events, or routing updates on Redwood's side? We can provide traceroutes or packet captures on request.

Thanks,
Carla Reed
Director of Engineering, BluePeak Health
Carla.Reed@bluepeakhealth.com

Attachments: none (we will send traceroutes if needed)

Hi Carla — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the impact. I'm escalating this to our on-call engineering and CS teams now.

Actions I'm taking immediately:

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Carla Reed <carla.reed@bluepeakhealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: production latency spikes + 500s from Redwood Inference

Hi team — initial triage notes below (quick summary, see attached snippets):

What I looked at:
- Redwood edge logs for connections from BluePeak IP ranges (us-west-2).
- DNS resolution traces for model-host.redwood.net from our side.
- Recent infra change log (no scheduled deploys or config pushes in the window).

Findings:
- Edge side: intermittent 502/504 spikes correlate with periods where backend gRPC streams were abruptly closed (RSTs) and subsequent DNS retries.
- DNS: several NXDOMAIN/timeout windows captured from BluePeak-resolvable IPs — the origin appears on BluePeak's resolver side intermittently failing to resolve our regional hostnames.
- Network path: traceroutes submitted (attached) show ~12–40% packet loss to one of the transit gateway peers; RTT increases dramatically at the transit hop.

Hypothesis: something in the network path (VPC peering/transit gateway route or a corporate proxy/firewall on BluePeak side) is injecting resets or dropping long-lived TLS/gRPC sessions. The symptoms match middlebox behavior (proxy timeout, application-layer reset) rather than Redwood host instability.

Immediate mitigation suggestions:
1) If possible, temporarily bypass any corporate proxy for calls to Redwood IP ranges (we can provide exact prefixes).
2) Validate VPC peering/transit gateway route tables for any route changes and confirm there's no new blackhole/propagation issue.
3) If bypass isn't possible, we can fail traffic to an alternate Redwood region (us-west-1) and update DNS TTLs to point to a hosted fallback until BluePeak stabilizes their proxy rules.

Attached: traceroute-to-redwood-06-08.txt, redwood-tcp-dump-snippet.txt (shows RSTs).

I'll keep investigating route metrics and packet captures. Monica — can you coordinate rollback/fallback options with the customer and document a mutual action plan?

— Dylan (on-call infra)
From: Carla Reed <carla.reed@bluepeakhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: BluePeak NOC <noc@bluepeakhealth.com>, sanjay.patel@bluepeakhealth.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: production latency spikes + 500s from Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick update from our side after triage this morning.

What we found:
- Our security team applied a proxy rule change late last night to tighten long-lived connections through the corporate perimeter. That rule is terminating gRPC/TLS streams above a ~60s threshold and occasionally returning 502-type responses when the session is reset. That change was rolled to a subgroup of IP subnets that include some of the transit gateway peers used by Redwood.

Immediate steps we took:
- We applied a temporary bypass for Redwood's advertised IP ranges to stop the proxy from touching these flows (this reduced errors within ~14 minutes).
- We are reverting the aggressive timeout rule but need approximately 36 hours for controlled rollback and testing across regions.

Requests from BluePeak:
1) Can Redwood do an immediate failover to us-west-1 for our production pool while we fix the proxy rules? We understand this may involve brief reconfiguration/coordination.
2) We will need a formal incident summary and proposed credit for the downtime window; our CFO is asking for reconciliation and root cause.
3) We would like an exec-to-exec contact for the duration (our CEO and VP Ops are on the call tomorrow).

We're copying our NOC and Sanjay (VP Eng) on this thread. We appreciate the quick help — this was painful on our side because the change hit during a high-volume period.

Best,
Carla
Director of Engineering, BluePeak Health

Attachment: bluepeak-proxy-rule-change-diff.txt
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: Carla Reed <carla.reed@bluepeakhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: production latency spikes + 500s from Redwood Inference

Team — summary and proposal for exec:exec follow-up. Quoting the customer thread above.

Summary:
- Impact: BluePeak experienced ~6–7% 502/504 errors and p95 latency spikes (2.5–4.8s) on 2026-06-08 after a BluePeak-side proxy rule tightened long-lived connections, causing RSTs and DNS failures upstream. Customer applied a temporary bypass which reduced errors within ~15 minutes.
- Cause: Root cause is customer-side proxy policy that interferes with long-lived gRPC/TLS streams across the transit gateway/VPC peer path. No Redwood config deploys found in the window.
- Current state: BluePeak is rolling back the proxy rule (36 hours). They have asked for an immediate failover to us-west-1 while they complete testing. They also requested a formal incident summary and a credit for downtime.

Recommended Redwood actions:
1) Approve and coordinate a failover for BluePeak's production pool to us-west-1 as a stopgap. Tech owner: Dylan (on-call).
2) Offer a goodwill credit: propose 1 month of service credit against DF-4382 pending legal sign-off.
3) Provide an incident report (RCA) and postmortem within 3 business days.
4) Exec outreach: Sean Gallagher (VP Customer Success) to be primary exec contact for BluePeak; I will introduce Sean on the 09:00 PT call tomorrow.

Please confirm approvals:
- Dylan — can you confirm estimated ETA to perform failover and any risk notes?
- Sean/Monica — do we approve 1 month credit and exec outreach? If legal needs to review, loop them in; we want to be responsive given the board-level pressure on the customer's side.

I'll hold a short sync if needed. Carla — appreciate your partnership; we'll treat this as highest priority until rollback is complete.

— Rishi
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
